replies.author: zebleck
replies.body:
I'm giving myself a tight scope: get everything you can out of this asset pack and make it fun to play, in a very short time. My goal is not to reinvent the wheel here.

Don't underestimate speed. Lets say you want to try out a new idea, previously you would spend weeks building the prototype. Now you can get it in days and start iterating / finetuning.

In this case, I can start applying polish very fast, such as the effects system, fires, animations etc. and get them right early.

comments.author: sharkymcstevenson2
comments.body: Mind sharing some workflow tips? Been trying to get my RTS going as well

replies.author: zebleck
replies.body:
Sure what kind of RTS are you trying to build, are you using a game engine? I think it depends, in this case I think this specific kind of RTS is very suited to building with AI.

Some tips of the back of my head:

\- use claude code (opus 4.6) and codex 5.3. They're both beasts, Codex 5.3 even seems a bit more accurate in large complex codebases.

\- you can get really fast workflows using just HTML5 and node js. Claude is insane at one-shotting code. Claude/Codex didnt have to interact with a game engine which meant no constraints and we could design every system the way we wanted. Also means you can fuck it up more easily if the base architecture is not right.

\- you can iterate fast, build tech debt and then just refactor it later. Reworked the pathfinding system about 3-4 times, same with the rendering system until we got it to work.

\- Seperate functionality into digestible containers. For example the entire UI system was not immediately added, instead we built a ui-test.html page that contains every button / banner / healthbar etc. to just see if everythings right. Then let the AI implement it into the actual gameplay. Or for the fire system we first implemented a little editor in which we could test out different looks of the buildings on fire, then added it to gameplay afterwards. Keeps everything contained.

Now that im writing it down theres lots of little things that can go into it.

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body: Nice progress!! It is looking great! Have you experienced any problems or limitations to speak of? Seems like you are flying through it at a great rate!

replies.author: zebleck
replies.body:
Thank you for the kind words! I agree its absolutely crazy how fast you can build these days. What helped here I think is that I didnt use any game engine, just pure HTML5 and node js. That way the LLM doesnt have to work with game engine interfaces and can go straight to implementing. Also allows you to define an engine yourself that is perfectly suited to your game. 

  
There were lots of limitations I experienced like

\- it didn't understand how to implement a good pathfinding system. After struggling for hours I gave it resources about AOE 4's pathfinding and that sort of helped. However its still not perfect. AI has an issue with really complex mechanics in general (but its not impossible to implement with AI, just takes longer).

\- at the beginning I just gave it the sprite pack and just let it build the full RTS. Got a basic working prototype with correct animations, fighting, building and working multiplayer (which is INSANE!!) but: no collision detection, no real map, no real pathfinding etc. It was just very barebones, the base architecture was shit. So I thought the best way would be to first lay the base with the map editor, get that right, and then move on to gameplay. That worked out well.

\- Claude didnt understand exactly how the tiles in a spritesheet fit together. I had to tell it to imagine me as its eyes and basically tell me exactly what information it needs to understand how the spritesheet fits together. It gave me a form I could fill out, that worked

\- also generally a problem: the AI sometimes just misunderstands how a system should be built. But you want to build it fast so you just approve changes. Later you have to rebuild the system, which is fine, but a bit of a weird process. I rebuilt the pathfinding system and rendering system completely about 4 times each. At some point you also have to have a bit of a grasp about it, otherwise you wont make progress, because the AI wont understand whats going wrong. So basically, dont be afraid of tech debt to build fast, the AI can later rewrite the shit it has written before (with your help). Also the AI is afraid to rebuild stuff sometimes and wants to add hotfixes and tweaks A LOT, which can make it worse.

replies.body: Depends, a lot of the times they have different task contexts. Theyre also not running all at the same time all the time (because I cant reprompt them all fast enough). For example, one is working on the server brower, while you let another implement the fog of war system. Then at the same time you found some bug in gameplay, so you let another agent fix that. And so on.

replies.author: zebleck
replies.body:
Very nicely noticed. Had the same problem, and the breakthrough was realizing AI should not make the art, only code. This asset pack is human made, thats why everthing fits together. Claude helped me write the map editor and then from there we developed the gameplay!

I think if you want to get into this, get state of the art AI agents like Codex or Claude. And then, just play around with it! Try to get it to build stuff, see where it breaks ,get a feeling for it. You'll need a lot of patience, but that has always been the case in gamedev and coding.
